results.title: Gov’t tasks EXIM Bank to drive self-sufficiency in poultry production
results.content: Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson says the government has directed the Ghana Export-Import Bank (EXIM Bank) to work with industries to make the country self-sufficient in poultry and poultry feed production.

results.title: Gov’t to replace Petroleum Revenue Management Act with broader natural resource law – Ato Forson
results.content: Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson has announced plans to introduce a new law to regulate the management of revenues from Ghana's natural resources, including oil, gold, lithium and bauxite.

results.title: 2027 Budget: Gov’t allocates GH¢782m to Sports Ministry
results.content: Government has allocated GH¢782 million to the Ministry of Sports and Recreation in the 2027 Budget to support sports development and the welfare of people involved in the sector.

results.title: 2027 Budget: GH¢8.9bn allocated for new hospitals, completion of 35 Agenda 111 facilities – Ato Forson
results.content: The government has earmarked GH¢8.9 billion in the 2027 Budget for the construction and completion of hospitals, alongside investments in psychiatric care, mental health services and digital healthcare systems.

results.title: EXIM Bank to lead poultry sector financing under four-year programme from 2027 – Ato Forson
results.content: The Ghana Export-Import Bank (EXIM Bank) will become the sole financial institution responsible for financing Ghana's poultry sector under a four-year programme beginning in 2027.

results.title: Gov’t to merge MIIF and GIIF to establish Ghana Sovereign Wealth Fund – Finance Minister
results.content: The government plans to merge the Minerals Income Investment Fund (MIIF) and the Ghana Infrastructure Investment Fund (GIIF) to establish a Ghana Sovereign Wealth Fund aimed at improving the management and investment of the country's mineral revenues and strategic public assets.

results.title: Government to uncap Exim Bank levies to boost poultry production – Ato Forson
results.content: Government will uncap the levies allocated to the Ghana Export-Import Bank (Exim Bank) to increase its funding capacity and support local poultry production.

results.title: 2027 Budget: Gov’t to construct 10 multipurpose sports stadia in underserved regions
results.content: Government has announced plans to construct 10 new multipurpose sports stadia across underserved regions in 2027 as part of efforts to improve sports infrastructure and grassroots development.

results.title: SSNIT to build five-star hotels in Accra and Kumasi under new tourism plan
results.content: Government has announced plans to facilitate the construction of five-star hotels in Accra and Kumasi by 2030 as part of efforts to strengthen Ghana's tourism and hospitality industry.

results.title: “Your cash is ready, come for your money” – Ato Forson announces early redemption of GH¢29bn DDEP bonds
results.content: Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson has announced the early redemption of GH¢29 billion in Domestic Debt Exchange Programme (DDEP) bonds due in February 2027, assuring bondholders that their money is ready for collection.

results.title: Government allocates GH¢3.5bn to Youth Ministry, GH¢2bn earmarked for jobs and skills
results.content: The government has allocated GH¢3.5 billion to the Ministry of Youth Development and Empowerment in the 2027 Budget to support young people's participation in the economy, with a significant portion earmarked for employment and skills development programmes.

results.title: Gov’t to remove funding cap, free up GH¢1bn for youth employment programmes – Ato Forson
results.content: The government plans to free up an additional GH¢1 billion for youth employment and apprenticeship programmes by removing the cap on funding allocated to the initiatives.

results.title: Western rail line to be extended to Nyinahin in Ashanti, and Hamile in Upper West – Finance Minister
results.content: Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson has announced plans to begin constructing a railway line from Takoradi to Nyinahin in the Ashanti Region in 2027, as part of a broader strategy to expand Ghana's railway network, support mineral processing and position the Takoradi Port as a major trade gateway to the Sahel.

results.title: December in Ghana to remain tourism anchor as government targets year-round visitors
results.content: Finance Minister, Dr Cassiel Ato Forson, has assured that the December in Ghana initiative will remain a major anchor of the country's tourism industry as government commits US$1 billion to transform the sector into a year-round economic driver.

results.title: SSNIT to build four-star hotels in Volta, Central and Northern regions – Ato Forson
results.content: The Social Security and National Insurance Trust (SSNIT) is expected to construct modern four-star hotels in the Volta, Central and Northern regions by 2030 as part of government's plans to boost tourism across the country.

results.title: Government secures about US$3bn for Accra-Kumasi Expressway
results.content: Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson says the government has secured about US$3 billion for the construction of the Accra-Kumasi Expressway, with the funds held in a dedicated project account at the Bank of Ghana. Presenting the 2027 Budget Statement and Economic Policy to Parliament on Thursday, November 12, 2026, he said the account contained US$2.2 billion and GH¢9 billion as of November 11. “As of yesterday, 11th November 2026, the project account at the Bank of Ghana held US$2.2 billion and GH¢9 billion, together equivalent to about US$3 billion. The money is in the safe custody of the Bank of Ghana,” he said. Dr Forson said the funds had been secured ahead of the commencement of construction, describing the development as the fulfilment of a government commitment.

results.title: Government targets 100% local refining of small-scale sector gold by 2028
results.content: Government is targeting 100 per cent local refining of artisanal and small-scale gold by December 2028 as part of efforts to retain more value from the country's mineral resources.

results.title: Gov’t to invest US$1bn in tourism, culture and creative arts – Ato Forson
results.content: Ghana will invest US$1 billion in the tourism, culture and creative arts sectors as part of efforts to transform the country's cultural heritage, historical attractions and creative industries into a year-round visitor economy.

results.title: Ghana to establish 24-hour minerals processing enclave in Western Region – Ato Forson
results.content: Government has announced plans to establish a 24-hour critical minerals processing enclave in the Western Region as part of efforts to boost local value addition and reduce the export of raw minerals.

results.title: No new taxes in 2027 Budget as government moves to improve revenue collection – Ato Forson
results.content: Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson says the government will not introduce any new taxes in 2027, opting instead to strengthen revenue collection and improve the administration of existing tax laws. Presenting the 2027 Budget Statement and Economic Policy to Parliament on Thursday, November 12, 2026, he said the government's priority was to ensure that taxes already due were collected efficiently and fairly. “This 2027 Budget will not introduce any new tax. Our task is to collect what is lawfully due, close the leakages, and make the revenue system work better,” he said. “Taxpayers deserve clear rules, fair treatment, and timely decisions,” he added. Dr Forson announced plans to review and modernise several tax laws and administrative frameworks in 2027. results.title: Government to invest over $200 million in nuclear power readiness from 2027 to 2028
results.content: Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson has announced that the government will invest US$200 million in a 24-month nuclear energy readiness programme as part of efforts to strengthen Ghana’s energy sector and support its industrialisation drive.

results.title: These are the 8 pillars of the ‘New Economy’ in the 2027 Budget
results.content: Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson has announced a US$10 billion investment programme to transform the country's economy over the next four years, with a focus on expanding local production, processing raw materials, creating jobs and reducing dependence on imports.

results.title: Mahama says new cedi notes will bring Ghana’s history closer to children
results.content: President John Dramani Mahama says the new Heritage Series banknotes will give Ghanaians, particularly children, a closer connection to the country's history by showcasing prominent personalities, historic landmarks and cultural symbols.

results.title: GH¢29.8bn allocated to Big Push programme in 2027 to accelerate road projects – Finance Minister
results.content: Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson has announced an allocation of GH¢29.8 billion to the government's Big Push programme in 2027 to accelerate road construction and improve transportation infrastructure across the country.

results.title: Government to train more than 2,000 scientists for nuclear power transition – Finance Minister
results.content: The Minister for Finance, Dr Cassiel Ato Forson, says the government plans to train more than 2,000 scientists to develop local expertise for Ghana’s transition to nuclear power.

results.title: Government to invest $1bn in Pwalugu multipurpose dam, first phase expected by 2029
results.content: Government is planning to invest US$1 billion in the full completion of the Pwalugu Multipurpose Dam, as part of efforts to boost agricultural production, expand agro-processing and strengthen energy supply. Presenting the 2027 Budget Statement in Parliament, Finance Minister, Dr Ato Forson said the project will support large-scale vegetable production, aquaculture, irrigation and hydropower generation. results.title: Government targets self-sufficiency in sugar production by 2030
results.content: Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson says Ghana will pursue self-sufficiency in sugar production by 2030 as part of efforts to reduce dependence on imports and strengthen domestic agro-industrial production. Presenting the 2027 Budget Statement and Economic Policy to Parliament on Thursday, November 12, 2026, he identified the sugar industry as one of eight integrated agro-industrial sectors under the government's New Economy programme. “Ghana will pursue self-sufficiency in sugar requirements by 2030,” he said.

results.title: Gov’t targets aquaculture expansion to address 500,000-tonne fish supply gap – Finance Minister
results.content: The government plans to expand aquaculture production and restore marine and inland fisheries as part of efforts to address Ghana’s annual fish supply gap of about 500,000 metric tonnes.

results.title: Government commits GH¢30bn to New Economy Programme in 2027
results.content: Government is committing GH¢30 billion to its proposed New Economy Programme in 2027, as part of efforts to transform Ghana’s economic structure, expand businesses and create jobs. results.title: Ghana has struggled to sustain a shared economic direction after Dr Nkrumah – Ato Forson
results.content: Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson says Ghana has struggled to maintain a consistent economic direction since the era of its first President, Osagyefo Dr Kwame Nkrumah, limiting the country's ability to fully realise its economic potential.
